newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Morgan Stanley rates Telecom neutral.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley rates Telecom neutral.

text.p: International finance house Morgan Stanley believes Telecom New Zealand Ltd shares are only moderately undervalued at current levels, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.

In an April issue of its Asia/Pacific Investment Perspectives, Morgan Stanley gave Telecom stock an initial rating of neutral and a 12-month target price of NZ$7.00 a share. Telecom was trading at $6.44 on Monday morning.
"We believe the rapid earnings and dividend growth that have propelled Telecom to 27 percent annual growth since its 1991 initial public offering are largely over," Morgan Stanley said.
It said the company would now face greater difficulty in brushing aside competition while at the same time reducing costs.

Recent developments on interconnect and number portability should give the company's rivals the ability they lacked in the past to bring the fight to Telecom, resulting in lower prices, smaller market share and narrower margins than those seen to date, Morgan Stanley said.
It forecast net profit to be $737 million for the year to March 1997 and $823 million for the 1998 financial year. Telecom posted a net profit of $717 million for the year to March 1996.
